title: Why Clarkson’s Farm Is An Unlikely Inspiration For HoYoverse’s Cozy Game Petit Planet
description: When thinking of the creative inspirations behind HoYoverse's upcoming cozy lifesim, Petit Planet, there are some things that instantly spring to mind. The development team has already acknowledged whimsical influences such as the children's fable, The Little Prince, and comparisons to genre titan Animal Crossing: New Horizons follow the game wherever it goes. However, speaking to GameSpot during HoYoverse's recent media week in Seoul, South Korea, lead game designer Murphy revealed an artistic inspiration that caught us completely off guard: Amazon Prime's hit documentary reality series, Clarkson's Farm. When asked if the developers had looked at other works of children's media or childhood nostalgia when creating Petit Planet, Murphy explained that former Top Gear host Jeremy Clarkson's agricultural adventures in the British countryside had a heavy influence. "[Clarkson's Farm] shares a lot of inspiration about how planting and running a farm can bring pure joy to daily life. So I think that is a huge inspiration," she explained. For Murphy, watching Clarkson, an older novice, grapple with the reality of soil types, weather, and new machinery provided a glimpse into the human satisfaction that comes from cultivating living things and growing your own food. A genuine, unfiltered experience like that became an essential way that the team wanted farming and planting to feel for players in Petit Planet. Petit Planet is deliberately stepping away from traditional live-service gaming rhythms, especially the ones seen in some of HoYoverse's other titles. Genshin Impact and Honkai Star Rail feature huge conflicts and overpowered protagonists, but Petit Planet is deliberately stripped of those high-stakes experiences in favor of an experience that feels more like everyday routine. Tending to your land in Petit Planet isn't a chore to maximize your output. Instead, it's a relaxing gameplay loop. While you may still associate HoYoverse with celestial gods and intricate…

title: The Xbox 25th Anniversary Console Restock Sold Out Before You Could Finish Reading This Headline
description: After quickly selling out earlier this year, Microsoft dropped a limited number of its 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X consoles for sale this week-- aaaaannnd they're already gone. Easily the best-looking Xbox Series X console thanks to its transparent green case, it looks like the majority of people looking to get one of these are out of luck, unless they're willing to pony up and pay extra for one of these consoles on sites like eBay, where they're currently being listed at next-gen console prices. Naturally, fans who missed out are livid, and online, they're calling out Xbox's first-come first-serve business model for selling the console, as opposed to a method like a lottery system that would even the playing field. Several disappointed buyers say that scalpers and bots go to all the remaining stock first, as they claim that it was sold out within seconds once again. People are especially mad at GameStop, as its dynamic pricing system had the console up for sale at the eye-watering price of $4,950, not including tax. Over on eBay, beggars can't be choosers, as people continue to pay an inflated price for this Xbox Series X. Sales of it are averaging around $2,500 per console, a significant mark-up from the $900 MSRP of the device. In comparison, both Nintendo and Sony have implemented lottery and queue-based reservation systems in the past, specifically designed to thwart scalpers and filter out automated bots. Last year for the rollout of the Switch 2 in Japan, Nintendo utilized an official lottery system via the My Nintendo Store, which saw over 2 million people enter. In western markets, Nintendo offered a direct invitation queue via regional Nintendo Accounts for verified active account holders. Sony's PS5 Pro has also become a hot item ahead of the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, and recently, Sony instituted an anti-scalping lottery system via the official Sony Store in Japan. To qualify for the draw, entrants were required to have a Japanese PlayStation…

title: Get Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater And All Bonus DLC Cheaper Than The Standard Edition Right Now
description: I don’t think there’s ever been a more iconic sound than the ‘!’ noise that triggers when you’re spotted in Metal Gear Solid. Even when I was a little kid, my first exposure to the franchise was through the Mesal Gear Solid: Snake Escape minigame in Ape Escape 3. That’s not really relevant, besides the fact that it shares a similar name with Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater, a remake and an absolute blast that’s now cheaper than ever, with all DLC included. If you ask anyone who has played the series, there’s a good chance that Snake Eater might be their favorite. Personally, I’m a sucker for The Phantom Pain and, of course, Metal Gear Rising—but a majority of fans love this one, and I can’t blame them. A prequel to the rest of the series, meaning it’s a perfect jumping-on point for interested newcomers, you play as Naked Snake, sent to Tselinoyarsk, USSR, to complete Operation: Virtuous Mission. But, like any secret mission, things go awry. Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater is, narratively, the same game as the original, so fans shouldn’t expect anything too different from the 2004 version. Instead, the gameplay is fine-tuned with some quality-of-life changes, while keeping the stealth combat at its core the same. Just with a fresh coat of paint slapped on, of course. And I’m really underselling it with the fresh coat of paint line. Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater completely refreshes the original, bringing it up to modern standards, with every element across the board brought to the current generation. Naked Snake has never looked so beautiful, and even one look at different screenshots for a direct comparison will show you just how overhauled the experience is. In our Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater review, Tamoor said, while playing the game, “I wasn’t an adult yearning for the lost feelings that made me love Metal Gear Solid 3; I was the teenager living them for the first time again.” And, as an added bonus, that Ape Escape mission is still part…

title: “You Guys Are F***ing Idiots”: Jeff Kaplan Takes Aim At Blizzard’s Overwatch 2 Reveal
description: Saying Overwatch 2 has had a rocky road since its 2019 reveal would be an understatement, and former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan isn't a fan of how the game was first announced. Speaking to Gaming World Interviews, Kaplan didn't mince words about the BlizzCon 2019 opening ceremony, where Overwatch 2 was shown for the first time, as Blizzard promised numerous features it either walked back or didn't deliver. Kaplan said that from 2018 until his departure, he experienced constant friction with Blizzard's executive leadership over game direction, scheduling, and core game mechanics. This led him to confront leadership about the lack of a clear vision or business model for Overwatch 2, and to question the wisdom of announcing Overwatch 2 at the same time as Diablo 4. "I got in a huge fight with, at the time, it wasn't Mike [Morhaime]. I loved Mike, who was the president of Blizzard, and another president of Blizzard, my executive producer, over announcing Overwatch 2. I went into their office, I’m like, 'What are we doing? We don’t really know what this game is; we don’t know what the business model is. This is a huge mistake.'" According to Kaplan, the new executives "had a lot to prove" when they joined Blizzard. "They wanted to prove that 'Blizzard's back and Blizzard still has it.' And I'm like, 'You guys are f***ing idiots,' you know? I don’t know how else to put it, but after three years of just getting worn down and not agreeing with any of the decisions that were being made on the franchise and not feeling like I had agency anymore--like before it used to be like I'm the game director I get to decide the direction the game goes. And starting in 2018, I lost that, and after three years of fighting for it back, I realized this company belongs to these corporate people now, the Blizzard executive team, the Activision team." Kaplan left Blizzard in 2021, saying Activision Blizzard’s financial arm told him that if Overwatch didn't meet certain financial goals,…

title: Fable Is Looking A Lot Darker Than We Expected
description: Amid a modest 25th-anniversary celebration, Xbox dropped a new preview of the Fable reboot. This snippet — which runs for under four minutes — offers plenty of gameplay and a closer look at some of the ghoulish enemies you'll face, set in a slice of Albion that looks surprisingly grim compared to the lighthearted Fable teasers that came before it. "The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire," the video synopsis reads. "Here, they cross a threshold where the natural magic of Deepwood appears corrupted by an outside force, and they discover hints as to who or what could be responsible." One thing to note about this snippet of gameplay is that it's pulled from the PC build of Fable, with the settings cranked up to Ultra. It's a pretty good-looking glimpse of what you can expect from Fable next year, even if it feels different from its cheekier predecessors and more like a feudal action slice reminiscent of Control Resonant toward the end, with its red-hued aesthetic. Of course, four minutes of Fable doesn't tell the whole story, and with the main campaign alone estimated to take 20 hours to finish, that doom-and-gloom feeling probably won't be present throughout the entire game. Fable launches February 23, 2027, for Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC, with Playground Games primarily handling development. Turn 10 Studios also assisted with development, and following recent changes at Xbox, it was merged into Playground Games. In addition to Fable, Xbox also revealed that new Wolfenstein and Doom games are in development, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s open letter to the Xbox community suggested that future game development might be more reliant on AI.

title: Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes
description: Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!" But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole. title: Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In Production At MachineGames
description: The long-rumored Wolfenstein 3 has been officially confirmed to be in development at MachineGames. The news follows many hints and rumors of a third game in MachineGames' planned Wolfenstein trilogy, the franchise's first new entry since Wolfenstein: Youngblood in 2019 and its first mainline title since 2017. Xbox CEO Asha Shar posted the announcement as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, and Bethesda also shared the news in its own post. In a move borrowed from the film industry, the game announcement was accompanied by a look at Wolfenstein 3's script, showing that protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz is back and more fearsome than ever. Bethesda also shared a photo from a mocap session, confirming that actors Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson will return to reprise their roles as B.J. and Grace Walker, respectively. MachineGames has said that it always planned for a trilogy of Wolfenstein games featuring B.J., meaning Wolfenstein 3 will continue the story that started with The New Order in 2014. MachineGames, alongside Bethesda, has also released three Wolfenstein spin-offs: the prequel The Old Blood in 2015, 2019's Youngblood, which featured B.J.'s twin daughters as protagonists, and the VR experience Cyberpilot, also released in 2019. The studio took a break from the Wolfenstein franchise to develop 2024's critically acclaimed Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. We don't have any more details on Wolfenstein 3 at present, including a release window, but we'll likely hear more soon.

title: Candy Crush Is Celebrating Xbox’s 25th Anniversary With Halo, Fallout, And Doom Crossovers, Including Remixed Music
description: 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and it's been a tough year for the brand with mass layoffs, studio closures/divestitures, and game cancellations. But the celebrations are still going ahead, including an event from the Xbox-owned Candy Crush mobile game juggernaut. Announced today, Candy Crush Saga is marking the Xbox anniversary with a "Game On" season that brings items and elements from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom, Banjo-Kazooie, Crash Bandicoot, and Spyro into the game through a virtual pin-collection event. Additionally, the popular and recognizable music from some of those games is coming to Candy Crush in "unmistakable Candy style," developer King said. Behold, the Candy Crush Xbox anniversary pins. The Game On event runs now through December 6. Players earn the themed pins, including Master Chief's iconic helmet, by progressing through Candy Crush's various levels throughout the season. The pins are being released physically, too, and people can enter a contest at the Candy Crush website for a chance to win. In terms of the updated music, Candy Crush Saga is adding "Candyfied" versions of music from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom, and Banjo-Kazooie. You can check out a neat behind-the-scenes video below to see how composer Federico Truzzi worked with the developers at King to remix the songs with a Candy Crush flavor. The music was recorded by the German Film Orchestra Babelsberg and the Bulgarische Orthodoxe Chor Berlin e.V. choir. In other Xbox anniversary news, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma released a statement marking the milestone, and referencing how the future of gaming could be focused on AI and vibe-coding. Microsoft also released a new hub called Xbox Playback where you can see your biggest Xbox accomplishments over the past quarter-century.

title: New Doom Game Seemingly Announced In The Weirdest Way After Half The Studio Was Laid Off
description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced that id Software is officially working on a new game, believed to be another Doom title. This is happening after Sharma oversaw id Software losing half of its staff to layoffs that were part of the Xbox "reset." Id Software replied to Sharma's post on Twitter to provide a few more details on the new game, which the team didn't say was a Doom game, but everyone suspects it will be. The studio said it's "incredibly excited" about the new game, which is in the works at id's studios in Texas and Frankfurt. Hugo Martin, an id Software veteran, is directing the game--don't expect to see or hear about it soon, though. "It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on," the developer said. A scene from Doom: The Dark Ages. Reporter Tom Warren said in July that id Software was in the "early stages" of developing a new Doom game, so this news today isn't totally surprising. Sharma cut staff at id Software (and numerous other Xbox studios around the world) earlier this year as part of a "reset" of the Xbox business. Marty Stratton of id Software recently said the studio is "doing great," despite the mass layoffs. Id Software's latest game was 2025's Doom: The Dark Ages. The game's newest update is coming on November 16, adding the new wave-based Slaughter mode.

title: My Trip Down Xbox Memory Lane Should Be Celebratory, But Instead It’s Just Depressing
description: Like the other console makers (not to mention every other company mimicking Spotify), Xbox typically releases a personal annualized recap, letting you look back on what that year entailed for you. With this month marking the 25th anniversary of Xbox as a brand, the company has delivered a supersized version of that feature, the Playback Archive, letting you see your full Xbox history over that span. It should be a fun, celebratory thing. Instead, I find it depressing. This has been a rough year for Xbox. It's certainly not the first time that's been true in the company's history, but this is a whole different level of troubling (I yearn for the days when Kinect being mandatory was the biggest issue). 2026 for Xbox has seen layoffs, a clear directive to embrace generative AI, and studio shutdowns or divestitures that signal the days of Xbox helping a game like Psychonauts 2 or South of Midnight come into being are in the past. Even amid the ongoing BDS boycott of Microsoft, the reasons to no longer feel good about investing in Xbox are mounting. My Playback Archive dates back 23 years, to December 27, 2003, the day I bought an Xbox Live subscription at Media Play in order to play MechAssault and NBA 2K3 online. I still remember the thrill of that, even as someone who had spent plenty of time playing online games like Unreal Tournament and Phantasy Star Online. The notion that I had this single profile and access to a growing library of online games was exciting. A snapshot of my Xbox Playback Archive Xbox established itself as my go-to platform for the next few generations and 11,000-plus hours of playing time. Even with incomplete data in the Playback Archive, I'm filled with memories of playing Halo 2 and 3 online, embracing MOBAs with Smite, and the countless hours I lost to sports games that I've since abandoned due to time constraints and the creeping influence of microtransactions. I'm reminded of not just the systems and games Xbox got me to embrace, but all…

title: Games Will Have A Physical Footprint Forever, Take-Two Boss Says, But It’ll Be “Very Small”
description: It's no secret that the market for physical video games is drying up, but don't expect physical media for gaming to go away entirely anytime soon, or ever, according to Take-Two's Strauss Zelnick. He told The Game Business that it "may not be the end" for physical media entirely in games, even with Sony killing off PlayStation discs in 2028. He said there will "always be some physical business" for gaming, but it will be a "very small part of the business." Lucia and Jason in GTA 6. He likened the scale of it to the vinyl business for recorded music. Most people might stream music today, but the market for vinyl is still there--and it's growing. For Take-Two, however, Zelnick said its business today is 98% digital. Going all-digital has a lot of benefits for publishers, but it's mainly about making more money. For GTA 6, the most highly anticipated game release ever, Rockstar is not offering the game on a disc, but the game will appear in stores via a code-in-a-box version. GTA 6's $400 collector's edition comes with a range of physical goods (but not the game), and Rockstar is also releasing GTA 6's score on CD and vinyl, but the game itself remains a digital-only experience. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC edition and online multiplayer are both rumored to launch in 2027.

title: This Happy Ending For Two Games With Identical Names Was A Headache For Nintendo
description: On November 25, two entirely separate games called Piece by Piece are releasing on Nintendo Switch. It's no coincidence, but the circumstances that led to this unusual situation certainly stem from a coincidence. Publisher No More Robots launched Piece by Piece, a cozy sim game full of cute animal characters, on Steam back in March. Two days later, studio Neon Polygons self-published an unrelated puzzle-platformer where you jump through literal puzzle pieces that you connect together--this game is also called Piece by Piece. What could have been a conflict between indie developers turned out to be the beginning of a wholesome business relationship. Both games were bundled together on Steam, and now No More Robots is publishing the Switch ports of both titles. According to No More Robots co-founder Mike Rose, Neon Polygons "couldn't afford to bring their game to Switch," so No More Robots stepped in to publish the game for them. As with Steam, you can buy both games together in a bundle. It's undeniably a heartwarming and unique story, though one would assume that having to figure out the logistics behind launching two games that not only have the same name, but the same release date and publisher as well, was a nightmare on the backend of the Nintendo eShop. "And yes, Nintendo have ABSOLUTELY HATED THIS," Rose said in a social media post, adding that the publisher was questioned why it had two games with the same name "many, many times." At least the bundle doesn't also include the Pharrell Williams Lego movie Piece by Piece as well.

title: Disney Teases “Major Announcements” For The Game Awards
description: The Game Awards will air on Disney+ this year, and along with that, Disney has teased "major announcements and surprises" for its own games at the event. To be sure, The Game Awards will stream in other places, too, like YouTube and Twitch, so you won't need to sign up for Disney+ to watch. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney’s most anticipated titles in gaming," the company said. That's all that Disney had to say on the matter, but the tease has gotten people excited to theorize about the possibilities. For starters, Disney is already a big player in the world of video games, with nine different gaming franchises that have each generated at least $1 billion. One such franchise is Kingdom Hearts, and many are expecting news about Kingdom Hearts 4 soon. Beyond that, there are ongoing rumors about a new version of The Simpsons: Hit & Run. Another possibility is that Disney shares more about its partnership with Epic Games and Fortnite. “A number of launches coming up over the next two years … are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership,” Disney executive Dana Walder recently said. Disney could also share new details about its upcoming Star Wars gaming projects, including Star Wars Eclipse, or possibly the rumored Jedi 3 or Battlefront 3. Or Disney could show off some of its new Marvel projects, including the upcoming Iron Man game. Marvel's Blade also remains in development amid uncertainty about its developer, Arkane Lyon. Disney’s new CEO, Josh D’Amaro, is a big believer in games and has suggested gaming could be Disney’s next big growth-driver, after the company’s stock price has been flat over the past decade. Some have theorized that Disney could buy Epic and Fortnite to help grow the business, but nothing has materialized as of yet. The Game Awards are set for Thursday, December 10 from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Keep checking back with GameSpot for more.

title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Pays Tribute To A Classic, Non-Canon Manga
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is largely a very reverent remake, with new quality-of-life features and small tweaks. That goes for the story as well, which largely maintains the original and slightly expands or clarifies some sections. But it also appears to pay homage to a classic Zelda manga. The manga is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by Akira Himekawa, which itself was a retelling of the Nintendo 64 game. It was released in Japan in 2000 and first released in America in 2008, followed by an expanded Legendary Edition in 2016. This version of the story isn’t considered canon, as it took liberties here and there, but a couple of those have now been incorporated into the remake's story. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 2026 Ending Spoilers Follow Following the climactic battle against Ganondorf, his evil tower itself falls apart, with Link and Zelda escaping to safety. During this escape sequence in the remake, Link takes out his trusty hookshot to cross a gap, and does the undeniably cool hero maneuver of grabbing Zelda to pull her across with him. If you saw that and felt it was vaguely familiar, it's probably because you saw it in Himekawa's art, when Link pulls a similar move with Malon. Link crossing by hookshot panel comparison Subsequent panels make the parallels even more overt. When Ganondorf emerges as Ganon, he smacks the Master Sword right off of Link, forcing you to temporarily use another weapon to damage him. In the original Ocarina of Time game, you eventually stun him long enough to run over and retrieve the Master Sword, and get a little pep talk from Zelda. The manga made this story beat more dramatic, and Zelda more proactive, by throwing the Master Sword to Link. This appears to have been adapted directly for the Ocarina remake, right down to some of the shot composition. Zelda prepares to throw the Master Sword panel comparison "Link!
